judgment.rationale: Win+V clipboard-history handling sits outside the remapping path that Keyboard Manager controls.
evidence: The reporter and follow-up comments confirm that remapped Control/Caps behavior interferes with Win+V and produces Caps Lock plus V.
One comment says disabling Keyboard Manager removes the symptom.
The issue is labeled External Dependency in addition to the Keyboard Shortcut Manager area label.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep this parked as an external dependency unless Windows exposes a supported interception point that lets Keyboard Manager remaps participate inside the Win+V clipboard-history UI.

fix_assessment.rationale: The retained judgment indicates an external or unsupported input path; no PowerToys-owned fix workflow is warranted.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager remaps do not propagate into the Win+V clipboard-history experience, and the issue disappears when Keyboard Manager is disabled.
known_information: The issue is open and labeled Issue-Bug, Product-Keyboard Shortcut Manager, and External Dependency.
The reporter confirmed that the Win+V sequence still misbehaves after remapping Control and Caps Lock.
Disabling Keyboard Manager clears the symptom.
inferences: This looks like Windows clipboard-history handling rather than a PowerToys-owned input surface.
issue_context.analysis: The lightweight revalidation did not uncover a PowerToys-controlled code path that could make clipboard-history honor the remapped keys, so the issue should stay out of the active fix queue.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and comment history.
Checked the current labels and the reporter follow-up that disabling Keyboard Manager removes the problem.
